inputs.original_text: Revelation was included in lawsuit challenging practice of targeting people seeking to gain legal status as they leave immigration courts Sign up for the Breaking News US email to get newsletter alerts in your inbox Lawyers for ICE provided false information to justify arresting and detaining thousands of people who had attended immigration courts, according to newly filed court documents. Federal prosecutors said that lawyers for ICE acknowledged that an agency memo from May of last year gave no authorization for the arrests, court documents show , despite previously citing it to justify the arrests. Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: This wasn’t just a memo being misread. ICE lawyers relied on a document that gave no authority to arrest people leaving immigration court, yet thousands were arrested. The lawsuit is peeling back the cover story: the system appears designed to turn people seeking legal status into targets, while institutions invoke the law to disguise how they’re getting around it. The “paperwork mistake” explanation is exactly the kind of excuse that keeps the machinery protected.
